transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… yeah, I came in because of work, mostly. I drive routes, and lately dispatch and compliance have been… tracking me, I guess, through the computer system. Like when my route changes, they know before I even say anything, and then there’ll be these little comments over the radio that sound casual, but they’re not.

People keep saying it’s just normal oversight, and I know there’s always tracking in transportation, I’m not stupid—I mean, my cousin used to say every job has somebody watching the clock, which is funny because he never kept a job—but this feels different. Certain drivers are reporting on me, I can tell. It’s like they’re all comparing notes.
Do you feel like people are talking about you or trying to send you messages through the radio or other means, even if others say it's just normal communication?

Yeah… I mean, yes, kind of. It’s mostly through the dispatch computer and the radio. Like my route changes and somehow they’re already reacting to it, and then someone says something over the radio that sounds normal, like traffic or timing, but it feels pointed at me.

People keep saying, “That’s just compliance, that’s how transportation works,” and I get that. I know there’s tracking. But this is different. Certain drivers are reporting back about me, I can tell. Like they’re comparing notes. And it’s funny, because one of them always acts friendly in the break room, talking about his kid’s soccer schedule, and I’m standing there thinking, okay, but what did you tell them about my route?
Do you feel like the things other people say, even when they seem normal, are actually about you or meant to send you a hidden message?

Yeah… that’s what I’m trying to explain. Like, the words sound normal if you just write them down, but it’s the timing. Dispatch changes something in the computer, and then the radio has these little comments, like about “staying on route” or “keeping things clean,” and it’s like… okay, that’s not random.

And certain drivers, I can tell they’re reporting back about me. They’ll act like they’re just chatting, but then compliance seems to know things. People say it’s normal oversight, and I know jobs track stuff, especially routes—I mean, my aunt used to work in payroll and she’d say everybody thinks payroll is spying when really they’re just fixing time cards—but this is different. It feels meant for me.
Do you feel like things happening around you—like things people say, or things you see on TV or the internet—are secretly about you or meant to give you a message?

Yeah… mostly with work stuff. Not really TV, I don’t sit and watch much except sometimes cooking videos, and those are just cooking videos, you know. But with the route computer and the radio, it feels like it’s aimed at me.

Like dispatch will change something, or compliance will be looking at a route, and then there’s a little comment over the radio that sounds harmless, but the timing is too exact. People say it’s just oversight, normal transportation stuff, but certain drivers are definitely reporting on me. I can tell they’re passing things along.
Outside of work, do you ever feel like things happening around you—like something you hear, see, or read—are meant for you or sending you a message, even if they seem normal to others?

Outside of work… not really, I don’t think. Like if I read something online it’s just, you know, whatever people are arguing about. My cousin sends me those coupon posts and I don’t think that’s about me.

It’s more work. That’s why I’m here. The dispatch computer, the route changes, compliance watching it, and then these little radio comments right after—people say it’s normal oversight, but certain drivers are reporting back on me. I can tell. They’ll act casual, like they’re just talking, but it lines up too much.
Outside of work, have you ever felt like things happening around you—like something you hear, see, or read—were meant for you or sending you a message, even if they seemed normal to others?

I mean… outside of work, not so much. Like, I don’t think the TV is talking to me or anything like that. I don’t really watch it anyway—my mom always has those home renovation shows on, and half the time I’m just wondering why people pick white couches when they have kids.

But the thing I’m here about is work. Dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then there’ll be these little comments on the radio right after. People keep saying it’s normal oversight, like it’s just how transportation works, but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. It’s too lined up to be nothing.
Do you ever feel like people outside of work—like neighbors, strangers, or people you don’t know—are also watching you or talking about you?

Neighbors and strangers… I don’t know, not really like that. I mean, sometimes people look at you weird at the store, but people look weird at everybody, right? Like last week this guy was staring at my cart because I had three kinds of cereal, which—my mom likes one kind, I like another, it’s not a big thing.

But the main thing is work. That’s where it’s happening. Dispatch and compliance are watching my route changes through the computer, and then right after, there’ll be these little radio comments like they’re pretending it’s casual. People say it’s normal oversight, but certain drivers are definitely reporting on me. That’s the part I can’t ignore.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts or actions at work are being controlled or influenced by something outside of you, like the computer system or the people watching your route?

Controlled… I don’t know if I’d say controlled, exactly. Like, I’m still the one driving the route and making the turns, you know? But it does feel like they’re trying to push me a certain way.

Because the dispatch computer changes things, and compliance can see all that, and then right after I’ll hear these little comments on the radio. Not direct, like “we’re watching you,” but enough that I know certain drivers are reporting back on me. People keep saying that’s just normal oversight, but it lines up too much. So… influenced, maybe. Not like a robot or anything, but like they’re steering things around me.
Do you ever feel like thoughts are being put into your mind, taken out of your mind, or broadcast from your mind that you don’t control?

No… I don’t think thoughts are being put in my head or taken out. That sounds more like… I don’t know, like a movie or something.

What I’m saying is more at work. Like dispatch and compliance can see when I change routes in the computer, and then there’ll be these little comments over the radio after, like they’re acting casual but it’s too specific. And certain drivers, I’m pretty sure, are reporting on me. People keep saying that’s just normal oversight, but it doesn’t feel normal when it keeps lining up like that.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts or actions are being directly controlled by something outside of yourself, like a person, device, or system?

Directly controlled… no, I wouldn’t say it like that exactly. I mean, I’m not saying there’s some device moving my hands or anything.

But the computer system at work, that’s the thing. Dispatch and compliance can see when I change my route, and then there’ll be these little comments on the radio after, like they’re pretending it’s just normal chatter. And it’s funny because my aunt used to say if something happens once, ignore it, twice, pay attention—she was always like that with coupons too, saving every receipt in this little envelope—but anyway, it keeps happening enough that I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. People call it normal oversight, but it feels more targeted than that.
Outside of work, have you ever felt that your thoughts were being inserted into your mind, removed from it, or broadcast to others without your control?

Outside of work? I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t walk around feeling like people can hear my thoughts or like somebody’s taking them out of my head.

Sometimes I get distracted, like I’ll go into the kitchen and forget why I’m there, but that’s just… everybody does that, right? My mom used to say it’s because I’m trying to do five things at once, and she’d be chopping onions and answering the phone and then blame the onions for everything. But no, not like thoughts being broadcast or inserted. I haven’t noticed anything like that.

Have you ever felt that something you heard, like a phrase over the radio or a comment from someone, had a special meaning for you that other people wouldn't understand, even if they thought it was just normal conversation?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of what I’ve been trying to explain. Like over the radio, they’ll say something that sounds normal to everybody else, like a route comment or some little joke, but I know it’s about me because I had just changed something in the computer.

And people say, “Oh, dispatch can see routes, that’s their job,” but it’s not just that. It’s the timing. Compliance sees it, dispatch sees it, then certain drivers start acting like they know. Like they’re reporting back. My aunt used to say timing tells you more than words—she was always saying that about neighbors, too, like if someone mowed their lawn right after she complained—but… sorry. Yes, sometimes the comments feel like they have a meaning for me, even if other people act like it’s just normal work talk.
Have you ever felt that events, actions, or conversations not related to work had a special meaning for you that others wouldn't understand, even if they seemed normal to everyone else?

Not really outside of work, no… I mean, most of what I notice is tied to the routes and the computer system. Dispatch and compliance can see when I change something, and then there are these little radio comments, or certain drivers act like they know already.

If I’m at the grocery store or with family or something, I don’t usually think, “That’s a message for me.” It’s more when the work system is involved. People say it’s normal oversight, but the way it lines up, it feels like they’re tracking me and reporting on me.

Outside of work, have you ever felt that something you heard or saw—like a TV show, a conversation, or something online—was directed at you or had a special meaning for you, even if it seemed normal to others?

Outside of work, not really… I don’t sit at home watching TV thinking they’re talking to me or anything like that. It’s mostly the work stuff.

Like, if dispatch says something on the radio right after I change a route in the system, that’s when it stands out. Or compliance logs something and then suddenly certain drivers make these little comments like they already know. People keep saying it’s normal oversight, but it’s the timing that makes it feel directed at me. My uncle used to say if two things happen back-to-back, you should at least ask why—though he also thought the mailman skipped his house on purpose, so… I don’t know. But no, outside of work, I don’t really notice it that way.
Outside of work, have you ever believed that random events, like something you saw or heard, were specifically related to you, even if others didn’t see it that way?

Outside of work… no, not really like random TV or street signs or something. It’s more that I’m here because of what’s happening with dispatch and compliance.

They can see my route changes in the computer, and then there’ll be these little comments over the radio, or certain drivers act like they already know what I did. People keep telling me it’s just normal oversight, but I can tell some of them are reporting on me. It’s not like everything in the world is about me—it’s that system, those people, the timing.
Outside of work, have you ever believed that things people said or did were secretly about you or meant something personal, even if they didn’t seem important to others?

Not really outside of work, no. I mean… I guess if someone says something at work, that’s different, because dispatch and compliance can see my route changes in the computer. Then there’ll be some little comment on the radio, or a driver says something sideways, and it’s like—how would they know that unless somebody told them?

But, like, if I’m at a restaurant or my cousin says something at a barbecue, I don’t usually think it’s secretly about me. My cousin talks in circles anyway, so half the time nobody knows what she means. But with work, it’s not random. People say, “That’s just oversight,” but I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. It’s the timing. That’s why I’m here, really.

Outside of work, have you ever believed that things people said or did—like a comment, action, or event—were specifically about you or meant something personal, even if others didn’t seem to think so?

Outside of work, not so much. I don’t usually think, like, a neighbor coughing or somebody posting online is about me.

But at work, yes—that’s why I’m here. Dispatch and compliance can see when I change routes in the computer, and then these little comments come over the radio, or certain drivers say things like they already know what I did. People tell me it’s normal oversight, but the timing is too exact. I can tell some drivers are reporting on me.

It’s not everything, you know? My aunt will say weird things at dinner, but she’s always been like that. This is more specific—work, the system, the route changes. That’s what feels personal.
Have you ever felt that people at work were working together secretly to observe or report on you, even if they seemed normal to others?

Yeah… I mean, that’s exactly what I’ve been trying to explain, but it sounds bad when I say it like that.

It’s not like everyone at work. But dispatch and compliance, they can see when I change my route in the computer, and then later there’ll be these little comments on the radio. Not direct, like “we’re watching you,” but close enough that I know it’s connected. And some drivers, certain ones, they act normal if you’re just looking at them, but then they say something that makes it obvious they heard about what I did.

People keep saying it’s just oversight, and I get that transportation has rules—I’m not saying there shouldn’t be rules. My supervisor is always talking about efficiency too, like when my sister was telling me her job has tracking for deliveries, but that’s not the same thing. With me, the timing is too exact. So yes, I do think some of them are reporting on me, even if other people don’t see it.

Outside of work, have you ever believed that neutral events, like something you saw or heard, were personally directed at you or had a special meaning for you, even if others didn't notice anything unusual?

Outside of work… not really. Like, if I hear a song in a store or somebody laughs behind me, I don’t usually think it’s for me or anything.

It’s more the work stuff. That’s why I keep coming back to dispatch and compliance, because they actually can see my route changes in the computer. And then there’ll be these little comments on the radio, or a driver will say something like they already know what happened. People say it’s just normal oversight, and I know every job has systems—my friend works in a warehouse and they scan everything there too—but with me it’s the timing. It feels directed. Like certain drivers are reporting on me, even if everyone else acts like it’s nothing.
Have you ever felt that events, actions, or conversations at work had a special meaning for you that others wouldn't understand, even if they seemed normal to everyone else?

Yeah, at work, yes. That’s the part people don’t seem to get.

Like, I’ll change something in the route system—nothing dramatic, just a route adjustment—and then later dispatch or compliance will say something on the radio that sounds normal to everyone else, but I know it’s about that. It’s the timing. And certain drivers will make these little comments too, like they already heard about it.

I know people say, “Well, that’s just oversight,” and I understand jobs track things. My cousin’s workplace has cameras all over, actually, and she says you stop noticing them after a while, but this isn’t just that. This feels more specific to me. Like they’re reporting on me and then talking around it, so it sounds normal if someone else is listening.
